milestones.label: Srebrenica Genocide
milestones.source_notes: July 1995 (fall 11 Jul, killings 13-16 Jul: week 170); ICTY Krstić IT-98-33-T (2001) and IT-98-33-A (2004); ICJ Bosnia and Herzegovina v. Serbia and Montenegro (2007)

milestones.label: Country-wide ceasefire in force
milestones.source_notes: Ceasefire agreed 5 Oct 1995, in force on the morning of 12 Oct 1995 (week 183); BB1 p.429

milestones.label: Dayton Agreement initialled
milestones.source_notes: General Framework Agreement initialled at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base, near Dayton, Ohio, 21 Nov 1995 (week 189); signed Paris 14 Dec 1995; UNSC Res. 1022 (22 Nov 1995), 1031 (15 Dec 1995)

source_notes: War end: Dayton initialled 21 Nov 1995 (week 189) for a campaign ended by a signed settlement; ceasefire in force 12 Oct 1995 (week 183) for a campaign ended without one. Killed or missing: Research and Documentation Center (RDC), Sarajevo, June 2007 release: 97,207 killed or missing, of whom 57,523 soldiers and 39,684 civilians (the Bosnian Book of the Dead itself, published January 2013, splits differently). military_killed is the RDC table by army of service (ARBiH 30,906; VRS 20,775, a floor; HVO 5,919), a different table that does not sum to 57,523. Displaced: UNHCR estimate, about 2.2 million refugees and internally displaced. Territory: Dayton 51/49 (Contact Group 1994, Geneva Agreed Basic Principles 8 Sep 1995; GFAP Annex 2 Inter-Entity Boundary Line). No ceasefire-line share is carried until one is sourced to the standard of Sensitive History Design Gate §6. Srebrenica: 8,372 is the Srebrenica-Potočari Memorial list of names; the ICTY found 7,000-8,000 killed (Krstić IT-98-33-T).
